        adjoe builds the technologies behind mobile apps growth and monetization. With our core product Playtime Arcade<\\/strong>, we've become the global leader in rewarded advertising, an ad unit built on a simple premise: users earn real in-app rewards for engaging with new apps. The result is one of the most effective value exchanges in adtech, connecting advertisers and publishers with over 770 million users annually.<\\/p>

        Engineering the sub-millisecond decision engine that powers 200 million daily ad interactions
        <\\/strong>
        The Demand Core team builds the infrastructure that determines which of our thousands of active advertising campaigns are relevant to a user the moment they open our ad unit Playtime. At our scale, system latency is a business failure, downtime means advertisers stop spending, users stop earning rewards, and publisher revenue stalls. You will build and operate the services that power these decisions 200 million times every day<\\/strong>.

        Go microservices<\\/strong> load the active ad campaign catalog into memory, evaluating 40+ targeting constraints<\\/strong> and 30+ real-time signals<\\/strong>, geo, fraud status, budget caps to rank potential user performance in milliseconds<\\/strong>. Beyond campaign distribution, the team owns the entire ad interaction chain: processing clicks, views, MMP postbacks from Adjust<\\/strong> and AppsFlyer<\\/strong>, and in-app events that trigger rewards. These events are broadcasted through a hybrid messaging architecture using SNS\\/SQS<\\/strong> and Kafka<\\/strong>, directly powering our advertiser dashboards, publisher reward payouts, and ad campaign scoring pipelines, all backed by DynamoDB<\\/strong>.<\\/p>

        <\\/p>

        Your Mission & Who We Are Looking For:<\\/strong><\\/p>

        <\\/p>

        Production Golang Systems Expertise:<\\/strong> You bring 5+ years of backend development experience, including at least 3 years writing Go in production distributed environments. You will build and maintain our +99% Go microservice architecture\\u2014interfacing with our TypeScript\\/React frontend\\u2014to reliably handle 2+ million daily publisher interactions and scale beyond hundreds of millions of monthly active users.<\\/p>

        High-Throughput Event Streaming:<\\/strong> You have hands-on experience designing asynchronous microservice communication using event buses like Kafka, SQS\\/SNS, and Kinesis. You will build pipelines to collect billions of daily API events and aggregate them into our data lake for sub-second querying.<\\/p>

        High-Scale Data & API Optimization:<\\/strong> You understand database internals and low-level web standards (HTTP protocol, Encoding, Regular Expressions).         <\\/p>

        Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m\\/w\\/d)<\\/strong><\\/p>

        Regional Role \\u00b7 Remote, based in the DACH region \\u00b7 Reports to: Sales Director<\\/p>

        About Everfield<\\/strong><\\/p>

        Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.<\\/p>

        We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.<\\/p>

        The Opportunity<\\/strong><\\/p>

        The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.<\\/p>

        This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.<\\/p>

        Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.<\\/p>

        How the Role Operates<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Two levels, one standard.<\\/strong> The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Direct team leadership where it is needed.<\\/strong> Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 You are not a seller.<\\/strong> You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Reporting.<\\/strong> You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.<\\/p>

        What You Will Do<\\/strong><\\/p>

        Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Lead deal\\/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.<\\/p>

        Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.<\\/p>

        Revenue Standards & Definitions<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.<\\/p>

        Commercial Governance<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Support commission structure alignment with business goals.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.<\\/p>

        Commercial Diagnostics<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans.<\\/p>

        CEO & General Director Partnership<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required.<\\/p>

        What Success Looks Like<\\/strong><\\/p>

        In the first 12 months:<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again.<\\/p>

        What We Are Looking For<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. European B2B SaaS market experience required.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Commercial finance literacy is a strong advantage: reading a P&L, understanding revenue recognition, and being able to argue the return on a commercial investment.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Private-equity-backed or multi-entity SaaS environment experience is a strong advantage.<\\/p>

        Skills<\\/strong><\\/p>

        \\u2022 Structured coaching and seller development:<\\/strong> designing and running structured 1:1s, deal reviews, and field accompaniment to build individual seller capability, not just inspect opportunities.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Pipeline discipline and forecasting:<\\/strong> reading a pipeline critically, identifying risk early, and improving forecast reliability.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Change management:<\\/strong> driving commercial process adoption across multiple teams, and building momentum without relying on formal authority.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Documentation and knowledge scale:<\\/strong> writing down what you diagnose and what you implement, in a form another person can pick up and run. Work that lives only in conversation does not scale across a portfolio, and anything you build for one Business Unit should be reusable in the next.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Commercial planning and challenge:<\\/strong> building a bottom-up view of what revenue targets are achievable, pressure-testing top-down assumptions, and presenting credible alternatives to leadership.<\\/p>

        \\u2022 Commercial storytelling:<\\/strong> presenting clear, honest risk assessments to CEOs and senior leadership, and leading a review that drives decisions rather than just restating numbers.<\\/p>

        • Full Business proficiency in German and English is a must<\\/strong><\\/p><\\/li><\\/ul>

          Who You Are<\\/strong><\\/p>

          \\u2022 You lead teams and you influence without authority.<\\/strong> You will manage sellers directly in some Business Units and hold no formal authority in others. Both need to work. You build trust quickly and drive change through credibility, clarity, and structured analysis.<\\/p>

          \\u2022 You are hands-on with sales execution.<\\/strong> You are comfortable stepping into real deals, reviewing opportunities with sellers, and diagnosing pipeline issues directly with the team, without needing to be the person closing.<\\/p>

          \\u2022 You combine analytical thinking with practical commercial judgement.<\\/strong> You interpret pipeline data, and you also understand the realities of getting deals done.<\\/p>

          \\u2022 You communicate clearly and directly.<\\/strong> You raise commercial risks early, with a recommendation attached, and challenge assumptions constructively, including when performance doesn't meet expectations.<\\/p>

          You are pragmatic in complex environments.<\\/strong> Portfolio companies vary in maturity and commercial model. You bring discipline without imposing rigid process that doesn't fit the situation<\\/p>

          Hiring Processs:<\\/p>

          TA screen (30min)<\\/p>

          Hiring Manager interview (90min)<\\/p>

          Group Director interview <\\/p>
